## workflow doctor

Report the repository, tooling, and configuration in effect

### Synopsis

Report the git repository this session is in, which external
programs are installed, where the store keeps its files — or why it
keeps none — which .workflow.json is in effect, and which
required fields are still empty.

Makes no network calls by default, so it is safe to run anywhere and
tells you only that a credential is present. Add --online to ask Jira,
your forge and Slack whether each credential works; a webhook is left
unchecked. Add --json for the same facts as data, with the same masking.

```
workflow doctor [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  workflow doctor --online                              # ask each service whether its credential works
  workflow --request-log requests.log doctor --online   # a bug report's evidence
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help     help for doctor
  -j, --json     print the report as JSON
      --online   ask Jira, the forge and Slack if each credential works (not a webhook)
```

```
  -n, --dry-run             hold back every write to Jira, the forge, the messaging service, Taskwarrior, git and files, and say what it would have done
      --log-format FORMAT   say what goes to stderr as FORMAT: text, or json or logfmt, an entry a line stamped with its time (default text)
  -q, --quiet               say only warnings, errors and questions on stderr, leaving every note out
      --request-log FILE    append a one-line outline of each request (method, path, status, duration) to FILE, for a bug report
      --verbose             also say each request's outline on stderr, as a debug line (not while the terminal interface draws)
```
